result.headline: Not handled: 100.00% errors, p95 44660 ms — 0 responses from 1 attempts (0 attempts/s offered). Failures happened before any response, so this measures the load path, not the server.
reasons: 1 of those failures were timeouts (100.00% of traffic).
p95 latency 44660 ms exceeds the allowed 1000 ms.
recommendations: No request got a response (0 completed, 0 bytes) — failures happened in the load path (proxy/Tor/network), so this result says nothing about the target server's capacity.
Tor carries ~10–20 concurrent users per circuit: drop concurrency to 10–20, raise timeoutMs to 30000+, and re-run. Hundreds of users through one exit node only queue and time out.

Check the rotation log: repeated "Tor control timeout" means the control port is unreachable (Tor Browser 9151 vs system tor 9051), rate-limited (NEWNYM needs ~10s between calls), or needs TOR_CONTROL_PASSWORD. Fix that before re-running.
Prove the proxy first with POST /api/test-proxy against https://httpbin.org/ip (an IP-echo endpoint), not against the target page — an HTML page cannot show the exit IP.
Latency percentiles are estimated from a reservoir sample of 1 requests (exact count/avg/min/max).
